snippet.title: Ghostbusters 2024 - Everything We Know So Far
snippet.description:
"Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire" is an upcoming sequel that continues the story from "Ghostbusters: Afterlife." It revisits the Spengler family and the original Ghostbusters as they face a new threat after defeating Gozer. The film explores complex themes like loss, betrayal, and resentment. Director Jason Reitman remains involved as a co-writer and producer, teasing the return of familiar faces like Vigo the Carpathian. The cast includes previous stars, such as McKenna Grace, Finn Wolfhard, Carrie Coon, Paul Rudd, Bill Murray, and others. Some fresh faces like Patton Oswalt and Emily Alyn Lind join the ensemble. The movie promises emotional depth, with characters dealing with challenging periods in their lives, especially Ray, portrayed by Dan Aykroyd, who grapples with resentment and feeling left behind. It introduces a new narrative post-Gozerian era, offering a fresh mythology for the characters. Director Gil Kenan hints at new, terrifying stakes and visual references in an interview with Empire Magazine, promising an unexplored direction for the franchise. The post-Gozerian era brings forth a new antagonist named 'Death Chill,' threatening New York City with frozen spirits that freeze everything in their path, causing a lethal ice age. This new villain can end life through fear alone, presenting a formidable challenge for the Ghostbusters. With a blend of nostalgia from familiar characters, a fresh narrative, and high emotional stakes, "Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire" aims to be a unique addition to the franchise. Fans anticipate uncovering the intricate storyline and the challenges awaiting their beloved characters in this novel installment.

snippet.title: Aquaman And The Lost Kingdom Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom, eagerly awaited by fans, faced delays and on-set controversies. Jason Momoa's Aquaman costume, sticking close to the comic design, showcased a darker, more mysterious version with notable changes in armor and gloves. The delays, fueled by Covid and cast controversies, allegedly involved a hostile on-set atmosphere, alleged clashes between Momoa and Amber Heard, and seven days of reshoots. There was controversy on set, which is rumored to be the reason why Amber Heard’s role was significantly cut. Despite the turmoil, a potential trilogy remains on the horizon. James Wan, expressing interest in directing a third film, values creative freedom and the ability to put a lot of himself into this creative world. Throughout his career, getting to direct a trilogy in any franchise would be a first for him. Jason Momoa's surprising role extended to writing a fifty-page treatment for the movie, revealing a vulnerable side to his career. He’s always wanted to be a writer, but has never gotten the chance to explore that side of himself throughout his career as an actor. Training for the film was intensive, spanning six months, involving swim training, lifting, and meal prep to ensure actors' physical readiness. Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom, despite setbacks, benefits from a dedicated cast, stunning wardrobes, and Momoa's personal investment in the character. The film's journey, from controversies to behind-the-scenes insights, underscores the resilience of the project and the commitment of those involved. snippet.title: Migration | Behind the Mic
snippet.description:
"Migration" is Illumination's much-anticipated film following a peculiar duck family on an adventurous journey in New York City. The movie encountered significant delays spanning five years, primarily due to Covid-19. The entire cast filmed everything in isolation while drawing inspiration from each other's performances, fostering a semi-collaborative environment during the movie's creation. Unexpectedly, the film faced a release date pushback from summer to winter, partly due to COVID-related production delays. Universal Studios aimed to capitalize on audience demand for summer-like entertainment during the colder winter months. Despite facing competition from other blockbuster releases, such as "Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom" and "Wonka," expectations remain high for "Migration" owing to Illumination's track record with successful films like "Despicable Me" and "The Super Mario Bros. Movie." Keegan-Michael Key, excited about portraying a Jamaican character, encountered challenges perfecting the accent, often slipping into an Irish tone, and requiring numerous retakes. Voice actors appreciated the freedom in animated roles, allowing for exaggerated expressions and overacting, contributing to bringing their characters to life. Moreover, the film incorporated real-life attributes of the actors into the characters they voiced, adding unique touches to the animated personas. Director Benjamin Renner, who had limited interaction with the cast due to the isolated recording process, influenced the voice and character direction, fostering a cohesive connection among the team. The film's detailed animation, genuine character portrayals, and the director's vision promise an immersive experience for audiences. Despite the extensive delays and seasonal release shift, "Migration" emerges as a promising addition to winter cinema, showcasing perseverance and dedication throughout its challenging production phase.

Eddie Murphy is a versatile actor known for his success across various movie genres. He's recently delved into holiday films with "Candy Cane Lane," reuniting with director Reginald Hudlin for a unique family holiday movie that combines jump scares, car chases, and kung-fu fighting with holiday spirit. Despite his comedic genius, Murphy wasn't entirely satisfied with his performance in "Haunted Mansion," a film that grossed $117 million worldwide. His iconic role in "Coming to America" generated a staggering $350 million globally and initiated a lasting friendship with Arsenio Hall. Paramount's request to cast a white person in the movie led to the inclusion of the hilarious Louie Anderson. In "Dolemite Is My Name," Murphy starred in his first biopic, playing Rudy Ray Moore, an underground comedian from the '70s. This experience inspired him with the idea that belief in one's work is crucial to your career. Murphy's versatility extends to action films, as seen in "48 Hrs," where he balanced comedy and drama effortlessly. Eddie Murphy's iconic role as Donkey in the "Shrek" franchise showcases his instinctive approach to acting, relying on gut feeling rather than extensive research. He even ventured into musicals with "Dream Girls." Although he was initially insecure about his performance and the role was considered a risk for his career, it ultimately ended up paying off. Eddie Murphy's filmography showcases his ability to excel in various genres, from comedy to drama, animation, and musicals, making him a true jack of all trades in the entertainment industry.

snippet.title: Silent Night 2023: A Movie Without Dialogue
snippet.description:
There was a time when all movies were silent. Of course, that was because they didn’t have the technology to add sounds to the video yet. But in the modern era, movies that take liberties with sound are few and far between. At least, not something as bold as having ZERO dialogue in a movie. And not just a silly romp. A violent, blood-soaked action movie based on a father getting revenge on his son’s killers. Silent Night does just that, and based on how over the top and wild the trailer looks, it’s gonna be a heck of an adventure to watch. Releasing on December 1, Silent Night looks like it’s a lot more than a no-dialogue gimmick. Joel Kinnaman stars as a John Wick-esque main character, who, after being shot in a drive-by shooting, loses both his son and his voice. So naturally, he decides to take out the entire crime syndicate that was involved in the shooting. He kicks butt and takes names. Although maybe not the name taking part, cause he can’t speak. Silent Night also sees the return of legendary action director John Woo. Woo hasn’t directed an American film in 20 years. snippet.title: Thanksgiving | Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
Eli Roth's long-anticipated Thanksgiving horror film promises a fresh twist on slasher movies, maintaining a strong nostalgic vibe. Inspired by classics like "Scream" and "Halloween," the film aims to blend genuine scares with fun and memorable kills, prioritizing a distinctive aesthetic. Each character's demise is designed to be an iconic slasher scene, and the production embraces campiness, even featuring fake trailers that pay homage to classic horror tropes. 

The plot follows a whodunit style, akin to "Scream," but adds a unique Thanksgiving theme that the horror genre has rarely explored. The story begins with a Black Friday riot culminating in a tragedy, leading to a Thanksgiving-themed serial killer terrorizing Plymouth, Massachusetts. What initially appears as random slashes soon reveals a deeper, revenge-driven motive. Regarding the gore, the film is expected to be gruesome, but not excessively so. Eli Roth intends to cater to a broader audience while outdoing the horror scenes from the fake trailers. It's a rated R film but won't push viewers to the extremes of nausea. 

The film's fifteen-year journey to the screen involved script revisions and the impact of the pandemic. Jeff Rendell, Roth's co-writer, played a crucial role in finding the right approach to the story. The project essentially treated the trailer as the sole existing element and built the script from there. With its blend of gore, camp, and a nostalgic yet fresh approach to slasher horror, Eli Roth's Thanksgiving has the potential to become a classic holiday horror film, offering a long-awaited treat for fans of the genre.

snippet.title: Biggest Box Office Flops So Far (2023)
snippet.description:
Box office flops are a sad reality for the movie studios these days, and 2023 provided little help when it came to movies that didn’t live up to their potential in earnings. Of course, for most of us, the thing that really matters is whether a movie was good or not. But to the studios? Not so much. They are all about the Benjamins, or whatever the nickname for hundreds of millions of dollars is. What’s wild is that several of the movies in this video actually earned a lot of money in 2023. And we mean, like, a LOT of money. But when you factor in how much they cost to make, and then to market, their net profits were pretty slim. And for the movie studios, that’s considered a flop, even if they didn’t actually lose money. And many of these movies actually got solid reviews from critics, and a lot of love from audiences. It’s a strange world, you know? Anyway, in this video, we’re taking a look at a few of the biggest flops of 2023, so far. snippet.title: Killers of the Flower Moon Cast experience
snippet.description:
"Killers of the Flower Moon" is a movie with deep personal connections for its cast members, particularly focusing on the personal ties to the Osage Nation, and the haunting unsolved family tragedies that persist to this day. The film features scenes with room for improvisation, such as one where characters discuss the white men's attractiveness despite their sinister intentions. These moments emphasize the trusting and loving nature of the Indigenous people at the heart of the story. The film holds personal significance for actor Yancey Red Corn, who drew inspiration from his father and uncle's efforts to negotiate on behalf of the Osage Nation in Congress. The movie also explores his great-grandfather's unsolved poisoning, reflecting the corruption of the era. The cast's indigenous actors were overwhelmed with emotion while walking the red carpet alongside their peers, hoping the film will spark discussions about Native history and missing Indigenous people. The decision to focus on the relationship between two characters, Bill and Ernest, rather than the "white savior" narrative originally proposed, brought a more personal and nuanced dimension to the film. Leonardo DiCaprio and Robert De Niro's real-life father-son dynamic added depth to their on-screen roles, while their strong bond also contributed to the project's success.
